title: When Do Options Help? Policy Necrosis and Redundant Coverage in Option-Critic
abstract: arXiv:2609.05508v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Option-critic learns options: sub-policies together with a learned rule for when each one hands control back. Its headline result is that performance improves as options are added. We explain that result, with theory and experiment. First, the termination rule option-critic learns by maximising return contributes nothing. When the termination test and the policy that picks options read the same values, the test fires at every step, so the learned rule is identical to always terminating. When that policy explores and the test does not, as in option-critic itself, the rule can block the exploration; there are instances where it suffers $\Omega(T)$ regret while always terminating holds to $O(\log T)$. Forcing termination at every step leaves the option-count curve intact. Second, the policy inside an option barely explores at all, so a state locks onto the first action that looked good and never updates again. We name this policy necrosis

translated_title: 选项何时有用？Option-Critic中的策略坏死与冗余覆盖
translated_abstract: Option-Critic（选项-评论家）方法学习“选项”：即子策略，同时学习一个规则来决定每个选项何时将控制权交回。其标志性结果是：随着选项数量的增加，性能会得到提升。我们通过理论和实验解释了这一结果。首先，Option-Critic通过最大化回报所学习到的终止规则实际上毫无作用。当终止测试和选择选项的策略读取相同的值时，该测试在每一步都会触发，因此学习到的规则与“总是终止”完全相同。当该策略进行探索而终止测试不进行探索时（正如Option-Critic本身的情况），该规则可能会阻碍探索；在某些实例中，它会产生 Ω(T) 的遗憾，而“总是终止”则能保持 O(log T) 的遗憾。强制在每一步终止后，选项数量与性能的曲线依然保持不变。其次，选项内部的策略几乎不进行探索，因此某个状态会锁定在第一个看起来不错的动作上，并且再也不更新。我们将这种现象命名为“策略坏死”。
tldr: 该论文通过理论和实验证明，Option-Critic中学习到的终止规则毫无作用（甚至可能阻碍探索并产生Ω(T)的遗憾），且选项内部策略几乎不探索会导致“策略坏死”，从而解释了性能提升实际来源于增加选项数量所带来的冗余覆盖。
en_tdlr: This paper proves theoretically and empirically that the learned termination rule in Option-Critic is useless (and can even block exploration, incurring Ω(T) regret), while option-internal policies barely explore, causing "policy necrosis," thereby explaining that performance gains actually stem from the redundant coverage provided by adding more options.
